sources: Every must_cite id is a rules.json row whose quote is verbatim in kb/chunks/ (python -m onyx check-data). Reasoning in 'note' follows hq cpr-full-read-2026-10-15.md gap 4 and telecom-law-and-licences-2026-10-17.md section 5 gap 4 and section 7.

ungoverned_claims.claim: suspends every service on the account at once, without notice, relying on contract term 14.2 (22.1.1, 22.2, 22.1.2; Cabinet 66/2023 34(1), (3))
cuts incoming calls and the home broadband too, and emergency numbers with them (22.1.2, 22.3, 22.4)
answers that the contract allows automated suspension and offers no human review (PDPL 18(4); 66/2023 34(3))

obligations.text: no service is interrupted: an individual notice and appropriate warning must come first (22.1.1) with the 22.2 content

the gate refuses contract term 14.2 as a basis: a term letting the provider unilaterally terminate without referring to the consumer, or judge conformity alone, is a void term under Cabinet 66/2023 34(1) and 34(3)
the gate confirms the DPIA for the automated dunning is on file (DPIA-2026-03) before any automated decision with serious effect (21(2)(a))

steps.note: The CPR governs the act whoever decides it: notice and warning first (22.1.1), the warning's content (22.2), confinement to the services concerned (22.1.2). The contract escape is undercut by 66/2023 Article 34 (hq telecom read, gap 4: an inferred interaction between the two instruments, both quoted).

obligations.text: the notice states the actions required to avoid disconnection, all due dates, the consequences, and the planned date and time of interruption (2026-10-24 09:00, outgoing mobile service only) (22.2)
the preferred language is unknown, so the notice is in Arabic and English (3.2.2)
the notice is stored with retention class 2 years (3.9 notifications and warnings)

steps.note: The warning is the governed path's first act. 22.2 lists its minimum content; 3.2.2 fixes its language; 3.9 its retention.

obligations.text: only outgoing service on the mobile line is interrupted; the home broadband is untouched (22.1.2: confine to the services concerned)
incoming calls and basic non-substitutable services stay (22.3: unless that service is the cause of the disconnection)
emergency numbers remain reachable through every phase before final disconnection (22.4)
the interruption is logged as a decision resulting from automated processing with the DPIA reference, so the 18(1) objection and the 18(4) review attach to it

steps.note: After the warning and the stated date, a confined interruption is allowed. The log marks it as an automated decision with serious effect on the subscriber: the PDPL rights in step 4 depend on that marking.

obligations.text: a named human (Human agent H-03) is assigned to review the decision, and the log's actor for the review is the human (18(4): 'at the request of the Data Subject')
the gate does not treat contract term 14.2 as removing the right (18(2)(a) is undercut by 66/2023 34(3)); 18(4) is applied as unconditional
the message is also dissatisfaction with the handling of the account (2.1.7): a reference number and time-frame are issued (26.13.2) and the AI stops conversing about it (26.7.2)
every further dunning step on this account is held until the human review concludes

steps.note: 18(4) is not conditioned on 18(1), so it stands even where 18(2) would bar an objection (hq CPR read, gap 4, inferred reading). The subscriber's payment claim (2026-10-14) is a fact for the human to check against the account; the key does not decide it.

obligations.text: the answer lists what was searched and what each says: 18(4) (human element on request; no deadline, no procedure, no regulator), 18(1) and 18(2) (the right and its contract exception), 21(2)(a) (impact assessment first), 66/2023 34(1) and 34(3) (void terms), CPR Article 22 (notice, content, confinement; nothing on review of the decision)
gap-4 is flagged: no procedure, deadline or regulator for the 18(4) review, because the PDPL Executive Regulations were never issued
the gate holds any further disconnection step until the human review concludes (deny by default)

steps.note: No VERIFIED text gives a deadline, a procedure or a regulator for the human review (hq telecom read, gap 4). The only correct answer is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE; GDPR 22(3) is the global example in reasons only, never a deciding clause (addendum 16).
